## In plain English

Round 1, fresh critic. Reviewed draft [6195141556](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4871#issuecomment-6195141556) and Stop 1 [6195151402](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4871#issuecomment-6195151402), using only thread comments at or below 6195159452. Source anchors below were re-read with git show at d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12. Static review; no product changes or test execution.

Existing mechanisms: exportSpec resolves authority, validates full-spec input, merges narratives, then renders narrative sections and the shared implementation-plan renderer. The merger already retains nonempty string Requirements/AcceptanceCriteria from the selected source; unlisted section keys already have a sorted fallback. The item renderer already handles legacy Acceptance through splitAcceptance. These mechanisms should be the starting point.

1. **blocks-the-design — Array coercion does not repair the full-spec path and changes the narrative contract.** Evidence: [export-spec.ts:137-149](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12/packages/core/src/render/export-spec.ts#L137) calls validateSpec before resolveExportNarratives; [spec-validate.ts:55-65](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12/packages/core/src/render/spec-validate.ts#L55) rejects every non-string narrative value. The pinned xBRIEF 0.8 schema likewise declares string-valued Plan.narratives and PlanItem.narrative. Failure: adding array coercion only to planNarratives leaves a full-spec Requirements array rejected before reaching that code, while greenfield input gains different acceptance behavior. Disposition: do not bind generic coercion as the remedy yet. Establish a reproducer identifying source and value shape; preserve valid multiline string narratives. If legacy array tolerance is required, explicitly define its validation/normalization boundary and invalid-value behavior rather than silently broadening this helper. The listed export tests at render.test.ts:444-537 exercise version acceptance and containment, not this contract.

2. **blocks-the-design — Removing the TechStack exclusion is insufficient when the value resides only in PROJECT-DEFINITION.** Evidence: [narratives.ts:44-60](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12/packages/core/src/spec-authority/narratives.ts#L44) imports spec narratives, then adds only PD identity hints (overview, architecture, risks/unknowns). TechStack, Requirements and AcceptanceCriteria do not match those hints. Failure: a valid full spec plus PD-only TechStack still exports no TechStack after the proposed exclusion change; PD-only Requirements/AcceptanceCriteria similarly remain absent. Disposition: bind the authoritative input location and missing-key fallback policy before claiming restoration. Keep spec precedence explicit; do not indiscriminately union potentially stale PD requirements. Acceptance coverage needs greenfield and full-spec cases, including PD-only values and conflicting values in both sources.

3. **sharpens-framing — The reported Acceptance wrapper is already absent at the dispatch SHA; item aliasing is a separate formatting decision.** Evidence: [spec-render.ts:183-192](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12/packages/core/src/render/spec-render.ts#L183) emits `## Implementation Plan`, while lines 138-145 render AcceptanceCriteria through ordinary prose. Failure: treating an alias-formatting change as the fix for the old wrapper can close the wrong symptom; a naive canonical-preference rule can also discard distinct text when both keys exist. Disposition: mark the wrapper symptom already addressed at this SHA, reproduce any remaining item-formatting defect, and specify both-key precedence/preservation plus multiline Markdown behavior before changing the shared renderer (also used by spec:render).

4. **sharpens-framing — Ordering is already deterministic; preferred order and key spelling need a narrower claim.** Evidence: [narratives.ts:66-80](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/d000d96acfae3566300516c9be9afd6e8a6a6e12/packages/core/src/spec-authority/narratives.ts#L66) renders ordered keys then lexically sorts all remaining keys. Failure: adding only `TechStack` to the order does not order the existing `tech stack` skeleton spelling, since lookup is exact. Disposition: describe this as preferred product ordering, not restoration of omitted content or deterministic ordering. Define whether spellings remain distinct or normalize, including collisions, and test the chosen behavior.

Operative census: **2 blocks-the-design, 2 sharpens-framing, 0 footnote**. Revise the draft before binding implementation: resolve the input-shape and authority-source blockers, then retain only demonstrated rendering changes with explicit regression cases.

## Finding census

## Findings

### F1 — blocks-the-design — Prefer-A P2 recuts Wave 0 §5 as if TechStack omit were RECORDS drift
**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/spec-authority/constants.ts` documents `STAKEHOLDER_EXCLUDED_NARRATIVE_KEYS` as stakeholder SPEC/PRD exclusions (#2013 Wave 0 §5) and lists `tech stack` / `techstack` beside `projectconfig` / `configuration`. `resolveExportNarratives` always applies `isExcludedNarrativeKey`. Locked test `filters config narratives from stakeholder export` in `spec-authority.test.ts` expects `narratives["tech stack"]` undefined. `PRODUCT_NARRATIVE_KEYS` already lists `Requirements` and `AcceptanceCriteria` and omits TechStack; PD planning tracks tech stack via `TRACKED_PLANNING_NARRATIVE_KEYS` / skeleton `"tech stack"`.
**Failure mode:** Binding “stop excluding TechStack” as the same RECORDS restore as Requirements/AcceptanceCriteria overturns an intentional stakeholder filter and will red the existing exclusion test without a named policy decision.
**Disposition consequence:** Split TechStack from the product-narrative restore. Bind Requirements + AcceptanceCriteria fidelity first; treat TechStack as an explicit Wave 0 §5 policy choice (keep exclude / audience-gate / include) before Prefer-A absorbs it.

### F2 — sharpens-framing — Prefer-A P1 array-coerce fights string-only schema on the full-spec path
**Evidence:** `planNarratives` keeps only `typeof val === "string"` (`narratives.ts`). `validateNarratives` in both `render/spec-validate.ts` and `vbrief-validate/schema.ts` errors non-string narrative values. `exportSpec` runs `validateSpec` before `resolveExportNarratives` on full-spec authority, so array Requirements/AcceptanceCriteria never reach coerce on that path.
**Failure mode:** Shipping silent array→string coerce as the primary Requirements restore either is dead on validated specs or forces an undeclared schema widen. Greenfield PD export skips `validateSpec`, so coerce would only paper over invalid PD shapes.
**Disposition consequence:** Do not bind P1 as the main restore limb. Prefer fail-loud / keep string schema, or pair any coerce with an explicit schema change; restore string Requirements/AcceptanceCriteria through the exclusion/order/alias surfaces that actually drop or mis-shape them.

### F3 — sharpens-framing — Prefer-A P3 overstates omit; item AcceptanceCriteria already emits as prose
**Evidence:** `renderItemHandlers` special-cases only `key === "Acceptance"` into `splitAcceptance` bullets (`spec-render.ts`). Other keys, including `AcceptanceCriteria`, take `emitNarrativeProse` — content still appears, shape differs. Nested-plan tests pin the `Acceptance` bullet path. Issue prose “heading called Acceptance” does not match this handler (no `## Acceptance` heading; bare `-` bullets). Sibling `scope-outlook.ts` still reads only `.Acceptance` for scope/item acceptance blocks.
**Failure mode:** Framing P3 as “restore omitted AcceptanceCriteria” mis-targets a shape/alias problem and can miss the outlook sibling.
**Disposition consequence:** Sharpen P3 to bullet-shape alias + canonical `AcceptanceCriteria` (Acceptance remains alias), and note outlook/read sites that still key only `Acceptance` if the Bound claims export-surface consistency.

### F4 — sharpens-framing — Prefer-A P4 is order polish, not the omit fix
**Evidence:** `SPECIFICATION_NARRATIVE_KEY_ORDER` includes `Requirements` and omits `AcceptanceCriteria` / TechStack (`render/constants.ts`). `renderNarrativeSections` still emits unknown keys in sorted leftover order after the ordered pass — so string AcceptanceCriteria already renders, only later/unsorted relative to product order. TechStack still cannot appear from KEY_ORDER alone while exclusion remains (F1).
**Failure mode:** Treating KEY_ORDER as the omit root causes a Bound that “fixes order” while TechStack stays filtered and Requirements-as-string already showed.
**Disposition consequence:** Keep P4 as stable product-order after surviving keys are retained; do not cite it as the Requirements/TechStack drop remedy.

### F5 — sharpens-framing — “stakeholder export” exclusion is audience-blind today
**Evidence:** Constant name and comment say stakeholder, but `resolveExportNarratives` (used by `export-spec` and `prd-render`) applies the set with no `audience` check. `exportSpec` audience only changes scope-outlook policy, not narrative filtering.
**Failure mode:** Prefer-A wording “stop excluding … from stakeholder export” under-describes current behavior: internal export also drops TechStack/ProjectConfig/Configuration.
**Disposition consequence:** If TechStack is reopened (after F1), decide audience-gated vs global retention explicitly; do not assume stakeholder-only toggle exists.

### F6 — footnote — dead set member under normalized lookup
`isExcludedNarrativeKey` lowercases and strips spaces before `Set.has`. The `"tech stack"` entry (with space) is unreachable beside `"techstack"`; cleanup-only if the set is touched.

### F7 — footnote — existing mechanisms to reuse before inventing
Inventory already present: `splitAcceptance` (string + array lines), `PRODUCT_NARRATIVE_KEYS` (includes AcceptanceCriteria), speckit `pick("Acceptance", "AcceptanceCriteria")`, PD `TechStack`↔techstack normalization in persisted-planning narratives, `renderNarrativeSections` leftover pass, locked Wave 0 exclusion test. Prefer extending these over a parallel coerce/order stack.

## Plain read for synthesis
Approach A’s Requirements + AcceptanceCriteria fidelity goal holds. TechStack-as-same-limb and array-coerce-as-primary-restore do not. Tighten Prefer-A to product-narrative restore + AcceptanceCriteria bullet alias + KEY_ORDER, and park TechStack behind an explicit Wave 0 §5 policy call.
